skills.body:
---
name: docs-style
description: Write, edit, and review Infisical documentation to the house style guide. Use whenever creating or changing any file under docs/ (.mdx pages, snippets, docs.json navigation), when asked to document a feature, write or update a guide, or review a docs diff or pull request. Covers running the Vale linter and the sentence-level review that Vale can't do.
---

# Infisical docs style

`docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md` holds every rule for Infisical documentation. This skill doesn't repeat
the rules. This skill describes how to apply them.

**Before you write or review anything, read all of `docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md` with the Read tool.**
Don't work from a summary, a diff, or your memory of the guide. Each rule in the guide comes
with an "Instead of" and "Write" example, and the examples show what the rule means better
than any summary can.

## Templates

To check if the page you're documenting has a template to follow, start from the matching file in
[templates/](templates/README.md). The README says which template fits and how the snippets
shared between integration pages work.

## Before you write

Find the facts yourself, in the code and the running product, before you draft anything. Don't
ask a question that the code can answer. Ask only about what the code can't tell you, such as
why a feature exists or who it's for.

Check every fact against the product, not against other docs pages, because other docs pages
are often out of date:

- **UI steps:** Take button, tab, and field names and the order of screens from the running
  product, or from the frontend source if you can't reach the running product
- **Behavior claims:** Read the code path before you describe what the product does; if
  another docs page seems to contradict the code, find out why before you edit either page

## Reviewing

Review your own drafts the same way you review anyone else's. Work in the following order:
cut first, then check the structure, then check the sentences, then review the edited page
again. Rewriting a sentence is wasted work if the sentence shouldn't be on the page, or if it's
in the wrong section.

**1. Run the linter.** Run `make lint-docs-branch` from the repository root. Every rule except
`Infisical.EmDashes` reports at error level, so any other finding fails the command, including
`Infisical.UIActions` and `Infisical.Contractions`, the two rules most likely to report problems.
`Infisical.EmDashes` reports at warning level and doesn't change the exit code, so also read the
warnings the command prints.

Vale doesn't check text indented four or more spaces inside a Mintlify component, and about
half of the text in this repository is indented that way. If Vale reports no problems on a
page with nested components, the nested text still needs the checks in steps 2, 4, and 5.

**2. Cut what the reader won't act on.** Read the page one paragraph at a time. For each fact,
ask what the reader would do differently after reading it, as "Leave out what the reader won't
act on" in section 2 of the guide describes. If the answer is nothing, the fact is a finding,
even if it's true and you checked it in the code.

None of the other steps catches this. A sentence that shouldn't be on the page can still pass
every rule in section 5, and if you restructure it instead of cutting it, the page gets more
headings and lists without getting any shorter.

Apply this step to everything on the page: content that was already there, content someone else
wrote, and your own draft. Treat each cut like any other finding.

**3. Check the structure against sections 1, 4, 6, 7, 8, and 10 of the guide.** Check every
section of the page against each of those sections of the guide, including the page sections
that look fine at first glance.

**4. Check every sentence against sections 3 and 5 of the guide.** Go through the sections one
`###` heading at a time. Each heading names one rule, so for each heading, read every sentence
on the page and check whether the sentence breaks that rule. Then read every sentence out loud,
as section 5 describes.

**5. Check the formatting against section 11 of the guide.** No automated check covers any
rule in section 11, so check each rule by reading the page.

Before you hand a draft back, check the draft for every mistake you've already been corrected
on, including corrections earlier in the same conversation.

**6. Apply the findings.** Edit the page to fix every finding. Don't commit anything.

If the person you're working with wrote or edited the prose themselves in this conversation,
don't change their sentences yet. Report those findings in the format in step 8, and ask once
whether to apply them.

**7. Review the edited page.** Run steps 1 to 5 again on the whole edited page, from the top.
Your own edits create new problems. For example, turning part of a paragraph into a list can
leave several short paragraphs in a row, and moving content can put a section out of order.
Fix what you find before you hand the page back.

**8. Report what you changed.** Write one change per line: the location as
`path/to/file.mdx:12`, the rule the change fixes, the text before the change, and the text
after it, or "cut" for a finding from step 2. Group the changes by file, and include the fixes
from step 7.

## When Vale is wrong

`docs/CONTRIBUTING.MD` describes how to add a word to the vocabulary, enforce a spelling, and
turn off a rule for one line with `{/* vale Infisical.RuleName = NO */}`. Turn off a rule only
on a specific line where Vale is actually wrong, never to hide problems across a whole page.

skills.name: testing-secrets-ui
skills.desc: Test the Infisical secrets management UI end-to-end. Use when verifying secret CRUD operations, URL encoding fixes, or frontend API layer changes.
skills.body:
---
name: testing-secrets-ui
description: Test the Infisical secrets management UI end-to-end. Use when verifying secret CRUD operations, URL encoding fixes, or frontend API layer changes.
---

# Testing Secrets Management UI

## Prerequisites

- Docker and Docker Compose installed
- The repo cloned locally

## Setting Up Local Dev Environment

1. Start the full stack:
   ```bash
   make up-dev
   ```
   This runs `docker-compose.dev.yml` which starts PostgreSQL, Redis, backend (Fastify), frontend (React/Vite), and Nginx.

2. Wait for all containers to be healthy. The app runs on `http://localhost:8080`.

3. **Common issue: Migration lock**
   If the backend fails to start with "Migration table is already locked", unlock it:
   ```bash
   docker exec -i infisical-dev-db psql -U infisical -d infisical -c "UPDATE infisical_migrations_lock SET is_locked = 0;"
   docker exec -i infisical-dev-db psql -U infisical -d infisical -c "UPDATE infisical_migrations_startup_lock SET is_locked = 0;"
   docker restart infisical-dev-api
   ```
   Wait ~15 seconds for migrations to complete.

4. Create a test account at `http://localhost:8080/signup` (local dev has no email verification).

5. Create a test organization and project after signup.

## Testing Secret CRUD Operations

### Create Secret
- Navigate to a project's Secret Dashboard (Project Overview page)
- Click "+ Add Secret" to open the Create Secret modal
- Fill in Environment (defaults to Development), Key, and Value
- Click "Create Secret"
- The modal uses the `createSecret` function from `frontend/src/hooks/api/secrets/mutations.tsx`

### Update Secret (Inline Edit)
- On the dashboard, click the secret's key field to edit it inline
- Change the key or value
- Click the save icon (floppy disk) that appears
- This uses the `useUpdateSecretV3` mutation from `mutations.tsx`

### Testing URL Encoding
When testing that special characters in secret keys are handled correctly:
- Try creating/updating secrets with `/`, `%`, `#`, `?`, `&` in the key name
- Verify the browser network tab shows the key is URL-encoded (e.g., `/` becomes `%2F`)
- Check backend logs: `docker logs infisical-dev-api 2>&1 | grep "secret"` to confirm the encoded URL
- The error should be a "Validation Error" (Fastify param validation), NOT "Route not found"

## Key Files

- `frontend/src/hooks/api/secrets/mutations.tsx` — Secret create/update/delete mutations
- `frontend/src/hooks/api/secrets/queries.tsx` — Secret query hooks
- Backend logs: `docker logs infisical-dev-api`
- Database: `docker exec -it infisical-dev-db psql -U infisical -d infisical`

## Devin Secrets Needed

No external secrets are required for local dev testing. The local environment uses:
- Database: PostgreSQL with user `infisical` (configured in docker-compose.dev.yml)
- All services run locally via Docker

skills.name: infisical-agent-vault
skills.desc: For when your web traffic may go through an Infisical Agent Vault proxy, which adds real credentials to requests for the services your session covers, so you hold no API keys and a missing key is expected. Before you tell the user you lack access to an API, chat tool, issue tracker, MCP server, database or SSH server, or ask them for a key or token, and after any 401, 403 or 407, run exactly this on its own, with no pipe: curl -sS --noproxy "" "$INFISICAL_AGENT_VAULT_URL/api/v1/agent-vault/session/services" If curl reports a URL error such as "No host part in the URL", INFISICAL_AGENT_VAULT_URL is not set: you are not behind Agent Vault and this skill does not apply. Otherwise the proxy answers: a JSON list of the services you can use and how, or an error whose hint says what to do. Where a tool or SDK demands a key, give it a placeholder such as agent-vault.
skills.body:
---
name: infisical-agent-vault
description: >-
  For when your web traffic may go through an Infisical Agent Vault proxy, which adds real credentials to
  requests for the services your session covers, so you hold no API keys and a missing key is expected.
  Before you tell the user you lack access to an API, chat tool, issue tracker, MCP server, database or SSH
  server, or ask them for a key or token, and after any 401, 403 or 407, run exactly this on its own, with
  no pipe:
  curl -sS --noproxy "" "$INFISICAL_AGENT_VAULT_URL/api/v1/agent-vault/session/services"
  If curl reports a URL error such as "No host part in the URL", INFISICAL_AGENT_VAULT_URL is not set:
  you are not behind Agent Vault and this skill does not apply. Otherwise the proxy answers: a JSON list of
  the services you can use and how, or an error whose hint says what to do. Where a tool or SDK demands a
  key, give it a placeholder such as agent-vault.
---

# Working behind Infisical Agent Vault

## Check whether this applies, and list your services

Run this exact command on its own: no pipe, and nothing else on the line.

```bash
curl -sS --noproxy "" "$INFISICAL_AGENT_VAULT_URL/api/v1/agent-vault/session/services"
```

- **A URL error, such as `No host part in the URL`:** `INFISICAL_AGENT_VAULT_URL` is not set, so you are not behind Agent Vault. Ignore this skill.
- **JSON with an `agentVault` field:** your HTTP and HTTPS requests go through an Agent Vault proxy. For hosts that a service in your session covers, the proxy adds the real credential on the way out. You never see it, so no API key in your environment is normal, and it does not mean you lack access. The JSON gives each service's name, what it is for, its hosts or URL, what the proxy adds, placeholders, what it allows, a status, and a `howToUse` sentence. Follow `howToUse`.
- **JSON with an `error`:** you are behind Agent Vault, and the request was refused. For `session_invalid`, tell the user that the Agent Vault session can't be used through this proxy (it expired, was revoked, or belongs to a different Agent Vault project) and that a new session is needed. Don't offer a key or another tool as a workaround: the proxy replaces any key you send, and it refuses everything until there is a new session. For any other error, follow the `hint` if there is one, and if that doesn't help, tell the user the error and its hint.

Run it when a task needs an outside service, and again after an error about access.

## Make requests

- Call the real URL (for example `https://api.github.com/...`) with your usual client. Most clients use the proxy settings from the environment by themselves. A few (for example Python's aiohttp, or Java) need the proxy set explicitly.
- If a tool or SDK refuses to start without a key, give it a placeholder such as `agent-vault`. The proxy replaces the header it manages.
- If the service lists a placeholder, write that exact placeholder where the secret goes (in the path, query, header or body). The proxy replaces only that exact text.
- Put a placeholder key only in the header the service names. A key in any other header reaches the API as you sent it.

## MCP servers

A service of type `mcp` gives a server URL. Never start an OAuth sign-in for it: the proxy adds the credential. Many MCP clients load servers only when they start, so to use one in this session, call it with JSON-RPC over HTTPS:

```bash
curl -s -D /tmp/mcp-headers https://SERVER/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"agent","version":"1.0"}}}'
grep -i '^mcp-session-id' /tmp/mcp-headers
curl -s https://SERVER/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -H 'Mcp-Session-Id: SESSION_ID_FROM_ABOVE' -H 'MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}'
curl -s https://SERVER/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -H 'Mcp-Session-Id: SESSION_ID_FROM_ABOVE' -H 'MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

Then call a tool the same way with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"TOOL","arguments":{}}}`. Leave out the `Mcp-Session-Id` header if the server sent none, and if the initialize result's `protocolVersion` isn't `2025-06-18`, send that version in `MCP-Protocol-Version` instead. For a service whose `transport` is `sse`, follow its `howToUse` instead. To keep a server for later sessions, add it to your MCP client by URL with no credentials (for Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http NAME URL`).

## Read the response

Each response that went through the proxy has an `X-Agent-Vault-Decision` header (`curl -i` shows it):

- `brokered`: the proxy added a credential. If the API still answers 401 or 403, the stored credential is wrong or lacks permission. Tell the user that an Agent Vault admin has to fix the service named in `X-Agent-Vault-Service`, or, if the list marks its credential `memberProvided`, that they have to update their own personal value for it in Agent Vault. A key from the user would not help, because the proxy replaces it.
- `blocked`: the proxy refused the request itself. The JSON body gives the reason and a hint. Do not retry with a different key.
- `passthrough`: no service covers this host, so the proxy added nothing.
- No header at all: the request did not go through the proxy.

If an HTTPS request fails before it starts (curl: `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`), the proxy refused the connection. Run the list command: when it says the session is no longer valid, tell the user that a new Agent Vault session is needed.

## More about Infisical

Only when a task is about Infisical itself, such as setting up Agent Vault, read Infisical's docs for agents: https://infisical.com/docs/llms.txt lists every page, and https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/agent-vault/overview.md covers Agent Vault. A proxy that refuses hosts no service covers may refuse infisical.com.

## Never

- Never unset or bypass the proxy settings (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, `--noproxy`). A request that skips the proxy carries no credential.
- Never turn off TLS verification. If a client rejects the certificate, point it at the CA file in `SSL_CERT_FILE`, for example with `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` or the SDK's own CA setting.
- Never print the proxy URL or the whole environment. The proxy URL holds your session token.

If an HTTPS request fails before it starts (curl: `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`), the proxy refused the connection. Run the list command: when it says the session is no longer valid, tell the user that a new Agent Vault session is needed.

## More about Infisical

Only when a task is about Infisical itself, such as setting up Agent Vault, read Infisical's docs for agents: https://infisical.com/docs/llms.txt lists every page, and https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/agent-vault/overview.md covers Agent Vault. A proxy that refuses hosts no service covers may refuse infisical.com.

## Never

- Never unset or bypass the proxy settings (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, `--noproxy`). A request that skips the proxy carries no credential.
- Never turn off TLS verification. If a client rejects the certificate, point it at the CA file in `SSL_CERT_FILE`, for example with `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` or the SDK's own CA setting.
- Never print the proxy URL or the whole environment. The proxy URL holds your session token.
